laws.k: domestic-workers|US|Fair Labor Standards Amendments of 1974 (domestic service)
laws.t: Fair Labor Standards Amendments of 1974 (domestic service)
laws.tp: Minimum wage and overtime for domestic workers; live-in workers exempt from overtime.
laws.s2: Upah minimum dan uang lembur bagi pekerja rumah tangga; yang tinggal di rumah majikan tidak mendapat uang lembur.

laws.k: domestic-workers|US|William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008, s. 203
laws.t: William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008, s. 203
laws.tp: Contract and protection rules for domestic workers of diplomats (A-3, G-5 visas).
laws.s2: Aturan kontrak dan perlindungan bagi pekerja rumah tangga diplomat (visa A-3 dan G-5).

coded.vl: General labor law applies, or a dedicated statute grants its core rights
coded.n: Federal minimum wage and overtime cover domestic workers since 1974; live-in workers are exempt from overtime. Several states have domestic workers' bills of rights.

coded.fn: Written contract in a language understood
coded.vl: Written contract required and provided in a language the worker understands
coded.n: A-3 and G-5 visas need a written contract in a language the worker understands.

coded.vl: Statutory minimum wage applies on the same terms as other workers
Periodic payment required, without further safeguards
Only a daily rest rule, or a longer limit than for other workers
coded.n: Overtime pay, but live-in workers exempt.
No federal weekly rest (some states, e.g. New York, provide 24 hours).

coded.fn: Keeping own identity and travel documents
coded.vl: Express right, or retention by employers prohibited with a penalty
coded.n: Document servitude is a federal offence.
A-3 and G-5 visas tied to one employer.
Recruitment fee bans for some visas and federal contractors.

coded.vl: Courts or labor tribunals on the same terms as other workers, or fee-free
coded.n: Courts and the Wage and Hour Division.

coded.vl: Included in the general social security system, including maternity
coded.n: Social Security covers domestic employees above an earnings threshold.

coded.fn: Protection from abuse, harassment and violence

coded.n: National Labor Relations Act excludes domestic service.

dec.ct: Supreme Court of the United States
dec.pe: Arizona and Pennsylvania denied welfare to non-citizen residents. The Supreme Court said treating lawful residents worse because they are not citizens needs strong justification, which was missing.
dec.pi: Arizona dan Pennsylvania menolak tunjangan sosial bagi penduduk bukan warga negara. MA menyatakan memperlakukan penduduk sah lebih buruk karena bukan warga negara butuh alasan kuat, yang tidak ada.

dec.ct: Supreme Court of the United States
dec.pe: Texas let schools charge or exclude children without immigration papers. The Supreme Court said this broke the constitutional guarantee of equal protection.
dec.pi: Texas membolehkan sekolah memungut biaya atau menolak anak tanpa dokumen imigrasi. MA menyatakan ini melanggar jaminan konstitusional atas perlindungan yang sama.

dec.ct: Supreme Court of the United States
dec.pe: Men who could not be deported because no country would take them were held for years. The Supreme Court said detention after about six months must end unless removal is likely soon.
dec.pi: Pria yang tidak bisa dideportasi karena tidak ada negara yang menerima ditahan bertahun-tahun. MA menyatakan penahanan setelah sekitar enam bulan harus berakhir kecuali pemulangan segera mungkin.

dec.n: Hoffman Plastic Compounds, Inc. v. NLRB
dec.ct: Supreme Court of the United States
dec.pe: A worker in the United States lost his job for supporting a union. Because he had no permission to work, the Supreme Court said he could not get the wages he would have earned, even though the employer broke the law.
dec.pi: Seorang pekerja di Amerika Serikat dipecat karena mendukung serikat. Karena ia tidak punya izin kerja, MA menyatakan ia tidak bisa mendapat upah yang seharusnya ia peroleh, walaupun majikan melanggar hukum.

dec.n: Case No. 2227 (United States): remedies for undocumented workers after Hoffman Plastic
dec.ct: ILO Committee on Freedom of Association
dec.pe: After the US Supreme Court denied back pay to an undocumented worker fired for organising, unions complained to the ILO. The ILO committee said the remaining remedies were not enough.
dec.pi: Setelah MA AS menolak upah tertunggak bagi pekerja tanpa dokumen yang dipecat karena berserikat, serikat pekerja mengadu ke ILO. Komite ILO menyatakan sisa pemulihan tidak memadai.

dec.n: Avena and Other Mexican Nationals (Mexico v. United States of America)
dec.pe: Mexican nationals arrested in the United States were not told they could call their consulate. The World Court said the US broke international law and must review their cases. Many were never reviewed.
dec.pi: Warga Meksiko yang ditangkap di Amerika Serikat tidak diberi tahu bahwa mereka boleh menghubungi konsulat. Mahkamah Internasional menyatakan AS melanggar hukum internasional dan wajib meninjau ulang perkara mereka. Banyak perkara tidak pernah ditinjau.

dec.n: Undocumented Workers v. United States (Report No. 50/16)
dec.pe: Undocumented workers injured at work or not paid in the US took their case to the Inter-American Commission. It said the US must give them the same labour protection as others.
dec.pi: Pekerja tanpa dokumen yang cedera atau tidak dibayar di AS membawa perkaranya ke Komisi Inter-Amerika. Komisi menyatakan AS wajib memberi mereka perlindungan kerja yang sama.
